policies.title: Vietnam: Resolution 44 twelve-country 45-day waiver
policies.summary: The twelve named nationalities remain visa-exempt for 45 days from entry under Resolution 44. The former 30-day interval after departure was removed; six-month passport validity and legal admission conditions remain.
conditions: Resolution 44 Article 1 applies to Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland regardless of passport type or entry purpose; this record covers ordinary visitor passports.

Article 20 of the foreigner-entry law requires at least six months of remaining passport validity for unilateral visa-exemption entry and no Article 21 ground for refusal. These requirements apply to each entry.

There is no longer a general requirement to wait at least 30 days after the previous departure before re-entering under the unilateral waiver. Law 51/2019/QH14 replaced Article 20 from 1 July 2020; the Ministry expressly confirms the interval's removal and the 2026 consolidated law retains the amended provision. This does not guarantee admission or authorize an overstay.
The ordinary British citizen passport scope does not include British National (Overseas) or other special British documents; the MFA table expressly excludes BNO passports.

The resolution's policy window is 15 March 2025 through 14 March 2028. This is distinct from the permitted stay on an entry and from the date of this source review. Work authorization, residence, transit, crew, special-document routes and individual admissibility remain separate.

allowedStays.label: 45 days from the date of entry
notes: Resolution 44 Article 1 and foreigner-entry law Article 31(1)(c) establish the temporary-stay allowance; passport validity and the resolution's policy end date are separate.

policies.title: Vietnam: Resolution 229 twelve-country 45-day tourism waiver
policies.summary: The twelve named nationalities remain visa-exempt for tourism for 45 days from entry under Resolution 229. The former 30-day re-entry interval does not apply; six-month passport validity and legal admission conditions remain.
conditions: Resolution 229 Article 1 names Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia and Switzerland. It expressly requires tourism purpose, regardless of passport type; this record covers ordinary tourist visitors, not an all-purpose exemption.
Unilateral visa-exemption entrants need at least six months of remaining passport validity and must not fall within Article 21 entry-refusal grounds, under Article 20 of the foreigner-entry law.

The former general 30-day interval after the previous departure was removed by the Article 20 amendment effective 1 July 2020. The Ministry's express explanation and the 2026 consolidated law establish removal, not merely omission from a visa table. Every entry remains subject to admission checks; no automatic extension or unrestricted repeated-entry entitlement is asserted.

Article 2 sets the policy window from 15 August 2025 through 14 August 2028. Article 3 ends the earlier Resolution 11 Poland/Czechia/Switzerland pilot from 15 August 2025; its package-tour confirmation condition is not carried into Resolution 229's replacement tourism waiver.

Passport validity, the 45-day permitted stay and the resolution's policy window are separate. Employment, residence, diplomatic/official privileges, transit, crew, special documents and individual security/admissibility rules are outside this ordinary tourism baseline.

allowedStays.label: 45 days from the date of entry for tourism
notes: Resolution 229 Article 1 expressly limits this waiver to tourism. The permitted stay is not passport validity or the resolution's policy window.
